They said to him, 'Well have you come, brothers.' Not knowing who was speaking to them, Longinus said to them, 'Why, brothers, are you troubled and as if from a great journey wearied?' They said, 'Hear our bitterness, for a decree has gone out against Longinus the centurion by King Herod, that if you do not bring his head, your heads will be given over to the sword. We have been seeking him for nine months and have not found him. Behold, you have heard the evils that have befallen us. If you know a certain Longinus the centurion, tell us.' The holy Longinus said, 'I do not know the man.' Coming into his house, they stayed, and he said, 'Tomorrow you will depart on your journey.' It happened in the morning, and the holy Longinus said to them, 'What is the reason for seeking Longinus with such zeal?' They said to him that he is sought by the king because he makes his kingdom unstable, persuading to worship the crucified Christ and the king of the ages. They were grieved and reasoning among themselves, saying, 'What shall we do?' The holy Longinus said to them, 'Do not be troubled, brothers, nor be disheartened; for I am the one you seek, the servant of God and Jesus Christ Longinus, to whom you were sent.' The men, hearing, were troubled and became speechless…

And the holy Longinus said to them, do not be disheartened, brothers, but let us eat and drink and go to the one who sent you, for I have sold my body to Christ, that I may buy my soul from him, and they, having heard these things, said to him with tears, no, but we, having gone, will make a defense for you to the one who sent us, for if you are truly Longinus, we also will die with you, and we do not do this to lead you away to the one who sent us, and seeing that they were compelled by the spirit of God, he said to them, if you have mercy on me, do thus, take my head and carry it to the king, and you will be without care all the days of your life, and they, having been afraid, did not want to endure, and he swore to them, entreating them to do this, and they, having been entreated for a long time, said to him, therefore intercede for us in your army, that it may not be reckoned to us as a sin, and he, having said that he would do this, they cut off his head, and having beheaded the holy Longinus, they carried his head to the king, and the tumult of the lawless ceased, and the head of the holy Longinus was being kept by the prefect Lucius, and the men of the village, where the holy one of God was, having taken the body, placed it in that village
pass_b_english: As they approached, they said to him, 'Well have you come, brothers.' However, they did not recognize the one speaking to them, so Longinus asked, 'Why, brothers, are you troubled and wearied as if from a long and arduous journey?' The men explained their situation, saying, 'Hear our plight, for a decree has been issued by King Herod against Longinus the centurion, stating that if we do not bring his head, our own heads will be forfeit to the sword. We have been searching for him for nine months, but to no avail.' They poured out their hearts, sharing the difficulties they had faced, and asked if he knew anything about a centurion named Longinus.

The holy Longinus listened to their tale and then invited them to rest at his home, promising that they could continue their journey the next day. The following morning, he asked them about the reason behind their diligent search for Longinus. They replied that the king was seeking him because Longinus was undermining his authority by persuading people to worship the crucified Christ, the king of the ages. The men were clearly distraught, unsure of what to do next. The holy Longinus, however, offered them words of comfort, saying, 'Do not be troubled or disheartened, brothers, for I am the one you have been searching for – the servant of God and Jesus Christ, Longinus.' Upon hearing this, the men were shocked and left speechless.

The holy Longinus addressed them, saying, 'Do not be disheartened, brothers, but let us eat and drink, and then go to the one who sent you.' He explained that he had sold his body to Christ in order to buy his soul from him. The people, upon hearing this, responded with tears, saying, 'No, we will go and make a defense for you to the one who sent us, for if you are truly Longinus, we will also die with you.'

They assured him that their intention was not to lead him away to the one who sent them. Longinus, seeing that they were compelled by the spirit of God, asked them to have mercy on him and take his head to the king, promising that they would be without care for the rest of their lives. However, they were afraid and did not want to endure. Longinus swore to them, entreating them to do this, and eventually, they agreed. They asked him to intercede for them in his army, so that it would not be reckoned to them as a sin. After he assured them that he would do this, they cut off his head. The tumult of the lawless ceased after the holy Longinus was beheaded, and his head was taken to the king. The head of the holy Longinus was kept by the prefect Lucius, and the men of the village, where the holy one of God was, took the body and placed it in that village.

φήσαντος αὐτοῖς τοῦτο ποιῆσαι, ἀπέτεμον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφα λήν. Ἀποκεφαλίσαντες
